questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs and humans perform very different functions. However, all of them are built of humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals and phalanges. This pattern is an outcome of
options: Convergent evolution
Divergent evolution
Analogy produced by a similar habitat
Inheritance of acquired characters
questions.explanation: The same basic structure has developed in different directions to suit different needs. This is divergent evolution, and it produces homologous organs. Convergent evolution works the other way, giving different structures that perform the same function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider two pairs of structures used for flight: (P) wing of a bird and wing of a bat; (Q) wing of a bird and wing of a butterfly. Considered as anatomical structures, how should P and Q be classified?
options: P is homologous, Q is analogous
P is analogous, Q is homologous
Both P and Q are analogous because all of them are used for flight
Both P and Q are homologous because all of them are wings
questions.explanation: Bird and bat wings are both modified vertebrate forelimbs built on the same humerus-radius-ulna-carpal-phalanx plan, so as forelimbs they are homologous. The butterfly wing has no such anatomical similarity and is only functionally similar, so Q is analogous. The trap is to classify by function (flight) instead of by anatomical plan and origin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In 1938, a fish caught off South Africa turned out to belong to a group thought to be extinct. To which group did this fish, the Coelacanth, belong?
options: Jawless fish
Lobefins
Cartilaginous fish
Fish-like reptiles
questions.explanation: The Coelacanth is a lobefin. Lobefins are fish with stout, strong fins, and they evolved into the first amphibians. It is not a jawless fish, and it is not a fish-like reptile such as the Ichthyosaurs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lichens can be used as indicators of industrial pollution because they:
options: grow faster in areas with heavy industrial smoke
turn dark in colour when exposed to soot
do not grow in polluted areas
absorb soot and keep tree trunks white
questions.explanation: Lichens fail to grow in polluted areas, so their absence signals pollution. Their loss from tree trunks in industrial England exposed the dark bark.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (event) with List-II (approximate time) according to NCERT.
List-I
A. Appearance of first cellular forms of life
B. Invertebrates formed and active
C. Seaweeds and a few plants existed
D. Sudden disappearance of dinosaurs
List-II
I. About 320 mya
II. About 65 mya
III. About 2000 mya
IV. About 500 mya
options: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
questions.explanation: First cells appeared about 2000 mya and invertebrates were active by about 500 mya. Seaweeds and a few plants existed around 320 mya, and dinosaurs disappeared about 65 mya.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about adaptive radiation in Australia is INCORRECT?
options: A number of different marsupials evolved from an ancestral stock within the Australian continent
Placental mammals in Australia also show adaptive radiation into varieties resembling corresponding marsupials
The resemblance of the Tasmanian wolf to the placental wolf shows that these two share a more recent common ancestor with each other than with other marsupials
Occurrence of more than one adaptive radiation in an isolated geographical area can be described as convergent evolution
questions.explanation: The Tasmanian wolf is a marsupial, so it is more closely related to other marsupials than to the placental wolf. Their resemblance is convergence driven by similar habitats, not a sign of close kinship. This is the key trap.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Wings of a butterfly and wings of a bird are analogous structures.
Reason (R): Wings of a butterfly and a bird are anatomically similar structures that perform different functions.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Butterfly and bird wings look alike and perform the same function (flight). However, they are not anatomically similar, so they are analogous. The Reason describes the wings wrongly on both counts, so it is false.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which hominin, with a brain size of about 1400 cc, used hides to protect its body and buried its dead?
options: Homo habilis
Homo erectus
Australopithecus
Neanderthal man
questions.explanation: Neanderthal man had a brain size of about 1400 cc and lived in the near east and central Asia between 1,00,000 and 40,000 years ago. It used hides for body protection and buried its dead.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pouched mammals of Australia survived, whereas many South American mammals resembling horse, hippopotamus and bear did not.
Reason (R): Continental drift kept Australian marsupials free from competition with other mammals, while the joining of South and North America exposed South American mammals to North American fauna.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Continental drift explains both outcomes. Isolated Australian marsupials faced no competition from other mammals, while South American mammals were overridden by North American fauna once the two continents joined.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Lamarck proposed that evolution of life forms was driven by use and disuse of organs, citing giraffes that elongated their necks while foraging on tall trees.
Statement II: Lamarck's idea of inheritance of such acquired characters is the currently accepted explanation for the long neck of giraffes.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Lamarck did explain the giraffe's neck through use and disuse, with the acquired elongated neck passed to offspring. NCERT states that nobody believes this conjecture any more, so Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Darwin's finches
(B) Tasmanian wolf and placental wolf
(C) Forelimbs of whale and bat
(D) Wings of butterfly and bird
List-II
(i) Similarity between members of two separate radiations in the same isolated continent
(ii) Radiation from a seed-eating ancestral form
(iii) Different structures of an insect and a vertebrate performing the same function
(iv) Same bone pattern modified for different functions in mammals
options: A-ii, B-i, C-iv, D-iii
A-i, B-ii, C-iii, D-iv
A-ii, B-iv, C-i, D-iii
A-iv, B-i, C-ii, D-iii
questions.explanation: The finches radiated from a seed-eater (A-ii). The two wolves come from the marsupial and placental radiations of Australia (B-i). Whale and bat forelimbs are homologous (C-iv). Butterfly and bird wings are analogous (D-iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are examples of homology?
(i) Hearts of different vertebrates
(ii) Brains of different vertebrates
(iii) Flippers of penguins and dolphins
(iv) Eye of octopus and eye of mammals
(v) Forelimbs of cheetah and human
(vi) Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
(vii) Wings of butterfly and birds
options: Three
Four
Five
Two
questions.explanation: Vertebrate hearts, vertebrate brains, cheetah and human forelimbs, and the Bougainvillea thorn with the Cucurbita tendril are homologous. That makes four. Flippers, octopus and mammal eyes, and butterfly and bird wings are analogous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A population is in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with two alleles. In this population, 16% of individuals show the recessive phenotype. What percentage of the population is heterozygous?
questions.explanation: Here $q^2 = 0.16$, so $q = 0.4$ and $p = 0.6$. The heterozygote frequency is $2pq = 2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.48$, or 48%. The 24% option is the trap of forgetting the factor 2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following was NOT among the gases released from the molten mass that covered the surface of the early earth?
options: Water vapour
Methane
Ammonia
Free molecular oxygen
questions.explanation: The molten mass released water vapour, methane, carbon dioxide and ammonia. Free oxygen appeared only later, when UV rays split water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Embryos of all vertebrates, including humans, develop a row of vestigial gill slits just behind the head. In which of the following groups is this structure a functional organ in the adult?
options: Amphibians
Fish
Reptiles
Mammals
questions.explanation: Gill slits appear in the embryos of all vertebrates, but they become a functional organ only in adult fish. Amphibians are a tempting distractor because their larvae breathe through gills, yet NCERT states gill slits are not found in any adult vertebrate other than fish.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The forelimbs of whale, bat, cheetah and human do different jobs. Yet all of them have humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals and phalanges. What does this pattern show?
options: Analogy resulting from convergent evolution
Homology resulting from divergent evolution
Homology resulting from convergent evolution
Analogy resulting from divergent evolution
questions.explanation: The same basic bone plan has been modified in different directions to suit different needs. This makes the forelimbs homologous structures produced by divergent evolution. Similar function is not the criterion here, because these limbs actually perform different functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Charles Darwin
(B) Alfred Wallace
(C) Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
(D) Thomas Malthus
List-II
(I) Work on populations that possibly influenced the idea of natural selection
(II) Observations made during the voyage of H.M.S. Beagle
(III) Evolution driven by use and disuse of organs
(IV) Independent, similar conclusions from work in the Malay Archipelago
Choose the correct answer.
options: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
questions.explanation: Darwin drew his conclusions from the Beagle voyage. Wallace reached similar ideas in the Malay Archipelago. Lamarck proposed use and disuse, and Malthus's population work possibly influenced Darwin. The common trap is swapping Darwin and Wallace.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following pairs are examples of analogous structures?
(i) Eye of octopus and eye of mammals
(ii) Flippers of penguins and flippers of dolphins
(iii) Sweet potato and potato
(iv) Forelimbs of whale and forelimbs of bat
(v) Hearts of different vertebrates
(vi) Wings of butterfly and wings of birds
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation: Pairs (i), (ii), (iii) and (vi) perform similar functions but differ in origin, so they are analogous. Sweet potato is a modified root, whereas potato is a modified stem. Whale and bat forelimbs, and vertebrate hearts, are homologous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, fossils are best described as:
options: Living organisms that have remained unchanged for millions of years
Remains of hard parts of life-forms found in rocks
Imprints of soft tissues formed only in volcanic lava
Organic molecules formed by electric discharge in a primitive atmosphere
questions.explanation: Fossils are the remains of hard parts of organisms preserved in rocks. Option 4 describes the products of Miller's experiment, not fossils.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hugo deVries proposed that mutations, rather than small heritable variations, cause evolution. Which option correctly pairs the plant he studied with the term he used for speciation by a single large mutational step?
options: Evening primrose – saltation
Garden pea – saltation
Evening primrose – genetic drift
Garden pea – founder effect
questions.explanation: deVries based his mutation idea on his work with evening primrose. He called speciation through a single, large, sudden mutation 'saltation'. Garden pea was Mendel's plant, and genetic drift and founder effect are separate factors that change allele frequencies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The bones of forelimbs of whale, bat, cheetah and man are similar in structure, because:
options: one organism has given rise to another
they share a common ancestor
they perform the same function
they have biochemical similarities
questions.explanation: These forelimbs are homologous organs with the same basic bone arrangement even though they perform different functions. They are inherited from a common ancestor, which is an example of divergent evolution.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q5)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The NCERT family tree of dinosaurs (Figure 6.2) links these extinct reptiles to which living modern-day counterparts?
options: Crocodiles and birds
Frogs and salamanders
Whales and dolphins
Sharks and bony fishes
questions.explanation: The figure traces dinosaurs to crocodiles and birds as their present-day counterparts. Dinosaurs themselves are known only from fossils, which makes them an example of extinct organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
In a large population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 16% of individuals show the recessive phenotype (aa). Consider the following statements:
(i) The frequency of allele A is 0.6.
(ii) 48% of the individuals are heterozygous (Aa).
(iii) The frequency of homozygous dominant (AA) individuals is 0.36.
(iv) Repeated migration of individuals from a different population into this one would leave its allele frequencies unchanged.
How many of the above statements are correct?
options: One
Two
Three
Four
questions.explanation: Since $q^2 = 0.16$, $q = 0.4$ and $p = 0.6$, so $2pq = 0.48$ and $p^2 = 0.36$. Statements (i)–(iii) are therefore correct. Gene flow adds or removes alleles and disturbs the equilibrium, so (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In 1938, a fish that was believed to be extinct was caught off the coast of a particular country and identified as a Coelacanth. Which country was it?
options: Australia
South Africa
Brazil
Madagascar
questions.explanation: The Coelacanth, a lobefin long thought to be extinct, was caught in South Africa in 1938. Australia is the trap because it comes up in the chapter for marsupials, not for the Coelacanth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Animal husbandry and plant breeding programmes are the examples of:
options: reverse evolution
artificial selection
mutation
natural selection
questions.explanation: In breeding programmes, humans choose which individuals with desired traits reproduce. This is artificial selection.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A population of 400 diploid plants contains 200 AA, 120 Aa and 80 aa individuals. Calculate the frequency of allele a from these counts. If a population of the same size and the same allele frequencies were in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, how many aa individuals would be expected?
questions.explanation: Allele a frequency is $q = \frac{120 + 2 \times 80}{800} = 0.35$, so the expected number of aa individuals is $q^2 \times 400 = 0.1225 \times 400 = 49$. The observed count of 80 differs from this expectation, which indicates the population is not in genetic equilibrium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about industrial melanism in England is INCORRECT?
options: After industrialisation, soot darkened tree trunks, so white-winged moths were easily spotted by predators.
In rural areas where industrialisation did not occur, the count of melanic moths stayed low.
After industrialisation, white-winged moths were completely wiped out from the industrial areas.
Moths that could camouflage against the background of the tree bark survived better.
questions.explanation: NCERT stresses that no variant is completely wiped out. Only the proportion of white-winged to dark-winged moths was reversed. The other three statements match the predation and camouflage explanation and the rural-area observation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The sum total of all allelic frequencies of a gene in a population is 1.
(ii) $p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$ is the binomial expansion of $(p+q)^2$.
(iii) In disruptive selection, more individuals acquire the mean character value.
(iv) Gene flow occurs when gene migration happens multiple times.
(v) The direction of difference between measured and expected allele frequencies indicates the extent of evolutionary change.
(vi) Darwin built his theory on Mendel's inheritable factors to explain the origin of variation.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii), (iv) and (v) are correct, so the answer is 4. Statement (iii) describes stabilising selection, whereas disruptive selection favours both extremes. Statement (vi) is wrong because Darwin either ignored Mendel's observations or kept silent about them.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Pasteur's 'killed yeast' experiment is INCORRECT?
options: In pre-sterilised flasks, no life arose from the killed yeast.
In a flask open to air, new living organisms appeared on the killed yeast.
The experiment dismissed the theory of spontaneous generation.
The experiment explained how the first life form originated on earth.
questions.explanation: Pasteur showed that life comes from pre-existing life, but this did not answer how the very first life form arose. That question was later addressed by the Oparin–Haldane hypothesis of chemical evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Suppose strict pollution control in an industrial area of England stops soot deposition. Over many years, whitish lichens grow back on the tree trunks. Based on NCERT's explanation of industrial melanism, what is the most likely outcome in the moth population?
options: Melanic moths will be completely eliminated within one generation
The proportion of white-winged moths will rise again, while melanic moths decline but are not completely wiped out
Melanic moths will turn white because the cleaner environment induces the colour change
The moth proportions will stay as they are, because selection cannot reverse a change once it has occurred
questions.explanation: Against a light lichen background, white moths are camouflaged and dark moths are spotted by predators. Selection would therefore again favour white moths, though no variant is wiped out completely. Colour is inherited, not induced by the environment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A graph shows the frequency distribution of a trait in a population before and after natural selection. After selection, individuals with the mean value become fewer, and two peaks appear at both ends of the curve. This pattern represents:
options: Stabilising selection
Directional selection
Disruptive selection
Genetic drift
questions.explanation: In disruptive selection, more individuals acquire the peripheral values at both ends of the distribution curve. Stabilising selection favours the mean, and directional selection shifts the curve toward one side only.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: About 15 million years ago, two primates, Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus, existed. Which statement correctly compares them?
options: Dryopithecus was more man-like, while Ramapithecus was more ape-like
Ramapithecus was more man-like, while Dryopithecus was more ape-like
Both were hairless and walked fully upright
Both had a brain capacity of about 900 cc
questions.explanation: NCERT states that Ramapithecus was more man-like and Dryopithecus was more ape-like. Both were hairy and walked like gorillas and chimpanzees.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A graph plots the number of individuals against the value of a trait. Before selection, the population shows a single bell-shaped curve with its peak at the mean. After many generations of selection, the curve has two peaks, one at each end of the original distribution, with fewer individuals near the mean. Which type of natural selection does this represent?
options: Stabilising selection
Directional selection
Disruptive selection
Artificial selection
questions.explanation: In disruptive selection, more individuals acquire peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve, which produces two peaks. Stabilising selection would sharpen the single peak at the mean. Directional selection would shift the single peak toward one side.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: According to Darwin, the variations that drive evolution are small and directional, and evolution is gradual.
Statement II: Hugo deVries believed that the minor heritable variations described by Darwin, rather than mutations, cause evolution.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Darwin's variations were small and directional, and his evolution was gradual, so Statement I is correct. deVries held exactly the opposite of Statement II: he argued that mutation, which is random and directionless, causes evolution, not Darwin's minor variations.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Humans have produced many breeds of dogs through intensive breeding. How is this used as an argument in support of evolution?
options: Each dog breed has become a separate species, proving that speciation is rapid
It shows that characters acquired through use and disuse are inherited
It shows that different structures evolve for the same function
If humans could create new breeds in hundreds of years, nature could do the same over millions of years
questions.explanation: Artificial selection shows that selection can greatly change a group within a short time, so natural selection could do the same over geological time. The breeds differ from one another but still belong to the same group, so option 1 is wrong.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Miller and other scientists ran experiments that simulated conditions on primitive earth. How many of the following were reported to form in these experiments?
Amino acids, sugars, nitrogen bases, pigments, fats, single-celled organisms
questions.explanation: Miller obtained amino acids, and similar experiments yielded sugars, nitrogen bases, pigments and fats, which makes five. No living cell was ever produced, since how the first self-replicating capsule arose is still unknown.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are factual observations on which Darwin's natural selection is based?
(i) Natural resources are limited
(ii) Population sizes are stable except for seasonal fluctuations
(iii) Members of a population vary in characteristics, even though they look superficially similar
(iv) Most variations are inherited
(v) Characters acquired during the lifetime through use of organs are passed to offspring
(vi) The earth is about 4000 years old
options: Three
Four
Five
Six
questions.explanation: Statements (i) to (iv) are the factual observations NCERT lists as the basis of natural selection. Statement (v) is Lamarck's discredited idea, and (vi) is a connotation of special creation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Embryological similarities among vertebrate embryos, as proposed by Ernst Heckel, are no longer accepted as showing that an embryo passes through the adult stages of its ancestors.
Reason (R): Karl Ernst von Baer observed that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Heckel's proposal was disproved by von Baer's careful study, which showed that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals. This observation is exactly why Heckel's idea was rejected, so R correctly explains A. The trap is to assume that the embryonic gill slits themselves are disputed; the slits are real, and only Heckel's interpretation was rejected.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: According to Darwin, fitness ultimately refers only to reproductive fitness
Lamarck explained the long neck of giraffes through the use of organs and the inheritance of acquired characters
According to deVries, mutations are small and directional, and evolution is gradual
Alfred Wallace, working in the Malay Archipelago, reached conclusions similar to Darwin's
questions.explanation: deVries described mutations as large, random and directionless changes that cause speciation in a single step (saltation). Small, directional variations and gradual evolution were Darwin's ideas, so the option attributing them to deVries is the incorrect statement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which feature of reptiles, absent in amphibians, helped them reproduce away from water?
options: Viviparity with the young protected inside the mother's body
Thick-shelled eggs that do not dry up in the sun
Stout and strong fins for moving on land
Eggs laid in jelly-coated masses in water
questions.explanation: Reptiles lay thick-shelled eggs that do not dry up in the sun, unlike amphibian eggs. Viviparity is a mammalian feature in this account, and stout fins belong to lobefin fish.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When we observe stars in the night sky, we are in a way looking back in time.
Reason (R): Light reaching our eyes from a star began its journey millions of years ago from trillions of kilometres away.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Stellar distances are measured in light years. The starlight we see now left the star long ago, so we see the star as it was in the past, and R directly explains A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: On the early earth, UV rays from the sun split water vapour into hydrogen and oxygen. What happened to the hydrogen so produced?
options: It combined with methane to form ammonia
Being lighter, H$_2$ escaped from the earth
It formed the ozone layer
It condensed to form the oceans
questions.explanation: Molecular hydrogen is very light, so it escaped from the earth. It was the oxygen, not the hydrogen, that went on to react with ammonia and methane and later contributed to the ozone layer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Homologous structures may perform quite different functions in different organisms
In divergent evolution, the same structure develops along different directions because of adaptation to different needs
Analogous structures arise when a structure inherited from a common ancestor is modified for the same function in the same habitat
Similarities in proteins and genes performing a given function point to the same shared ancestry as structural similarities do
questions.explanation: Analogous structures are different structures in different groups that evolve for the same function, so they are not inherited from a common ancestor. A structure inherited from a common ancestor and then modified is the basis of homology. The other three statements agree with NCERT.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Who disproved the embryological support for evolution proposed by Ernst Haeckel?
options: Charles Darwin
Hugo de Vries
Karl Ernst von Baer
Louis Pasteur
questions.explanation: Karl Ernst von Baer studied embryos carefully. He found that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals, and this disproved Haeckel's proposal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Analogous structures indicate that the organisms possessing them share a common ancestry.
Statement II: Analogous structures are not anatomically similar, although they perform similar functions.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: It is homology, not analogy, that indicates common ancestry. Analogous structures arise by convergent evolution in different groups. Statement II correctly describes analogy as anatomically different structures with similar functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When a section of a population migrates to another place and population, gene frequencies change in both the original and the new population.
Reason (R): Migrating individuals add new alleles to the population they join, and those alleles are lost from the population they leave.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Gene migration changes allele frequencies in both populations because alleles are gained by the receiving population and lost from the source population. R therefore directly explains A. If such migration happens multiple times, it is called gene flow.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Flippers of penguins and dolphins are analogous structures.
Reason (R): A similar habitat results in the selection of similar adaptive features in different groups of organisms, directed toward the same function.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Penguins and dolphins are different groups that live in a similar aquatic habitat. Selection in this habitat favoured flippers for swimming, so the flippers resemble each other because of function, not common descent. That is exactly why they are analogous, so R correctly explains A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are examples of evolution by anthropogenic action, as described in NCERT?
(i) Insects resistant to pesticides
(ii) Weeds resistant to herbicides
(iii) Bacteria resistant to antibiotics
(iv) Eukaryotic cells resistant to drugs used against them
(v) Variety of beaks in Darwin's finches
(vi) Diversification of marsupials in Australia
options: Two
Three
Four
Six
questions.explanation: Items (i) to (iv) arise from selection imposed by human use of chemicals and drugs, so they count as anthropogenic. Finches and Australian marsupials are natural examples of adaptive radiation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 revealed a stage of human evolution with a brain capacity of about 900 cc that probably ate meat. Which hominid was this?
options: Homo habilis
Australopithecus
Neanderthal man
Homo erectus
questions.explanation: The Java fossils (1891) revealed Homo erectus, which lived about 1.5 mya, had a brain of about 900 cc and probably ate meat. Homo habilis had 650-800 cc and probably did not eat meat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In England, collections made after industrialisation contained more dark-winged (melanised) moths than white-winged moths.
Reason (R): Industrial soot darkened the tree trunks and killed the light-coloured lichens, so dark moths were camouflaged from predators.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Lichens do not grow in polluted areas, and soot darkened the bark. Predators could easily spot white moths against this dark background, while dark moths survived. R therefore correctly explains the reversal in moth proportions described in A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Hardy-Weinberg principle is incorrect?
options: The expression $p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$ is the binomial expansion of $(p+q)^2$
When a drifted section of a population becomes so different that it forms a new species, the original drifted population acts as founders (founder effect)
Gene migration occurring repeatedly between populations results in gene flow
Genetic drift refers to change in allele frequency brought about by natural selection favouring the fittest
questions.explanation: Genetic drift is a change in allele frequency that happens purely by chance, not through selection. The other three statements agree with NCERT.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to Darwin, the term 'fitness' of an individual or population ultimately refers only to its
options: physical strength and body size
reproductive fitness, that is, leaving more progeny
length of life span
ability to modify its organs through use
questions.explanation: Darwinian fitness is ultimately and only reproductive fitness. The better-fit individuals leave more progeny and are therefore selected by nature. Strength or longevity matter only if they lead to more offspring.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the event in List-I with its approximate time in List-II.
List-I
A. First cellular forms of life appeared
B. Invertebrates were formed and active
C. Some land reptiles returned to water as fish-like reptiles (Ichthyosaurs)
D. Dinosaurs suddenly disappeared
List-II
I. 65 mya
II. 200 mya
III. 500 mya
IV. 2000 mya
options: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
questions.explanation:
The NCERT timeline gives the following dates:
- First cells: about 2000 mya.
- Active invertebrates: by 500 mya.
- Ichthyosaurs: about 200 mya.
- Dinosaur extinction: about 65 mya.
The common trap is confusing the 500 mya invertebrate date with the 2000 mya date for the first cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding 'evolution as a process versus a result' is correct as per NCERT?
options: When we describe the story of life on earth, evolution is treated as a process, and when we describe the story of the world, as a consequence of natural selection
When we describe the story of the world, evolution is described as a process, and when we describe the story of life on earth, as a consequence of natural selection
It is now clearly established that natural selection is only an end result and never a process
The world we see includes both successful and failed products of evolution in equal measure
questions.explanation: NCERT says evolution is described as a process when telling the story of the world, and as a consequence of natural selection when telling the story of life on earth. It also states that we are still not clear whether these are processes or end results, which rules out option 3; option 1 reverses the two cases.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs represents analogous organs?
options: Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
Forelimbs of whale and bat
Sweet potato and potato
Hearts of different vertebrates
questions.explanation: Sweet potato is a modified root and potato is a modified stem. They are different structures that perform a similar function (food storage), so they are analogous. The other three pairs are homologous structures that arose by divergent evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A figure compares the skulls of an adult modern human, a baby chimpanzee and an adult chimpanzee. Which conclusion is correctly drawn from this comparison?
options: The adult chimpanzee skull resembles the adult human skull more than the baby chimpanzee skull does
The skulls of the baby and adult chimpanzee are nearly identical, and both differ greatly from the human skull
The baby chimpanzee skull is more like the adult human skull than the adult chimpanzee skull
The adult human skull resembles neither chimpanzee skull, which rules out a shared ancestry
questions.explanation: The figure shows that the skull of a baby chimpanzee resembles the adult human skull more closely than it resembles the adult chimpanzee skull. Distinctly ape-like skull features develop later, during the chimpanzee's growth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hugo deVries put forward the idea of mutations in the first decade of the twentieth century. On which plant did he base this work?
options: Garden pea
Evening primrose
Snapdragon
Bougainvillea
questions.explanation: deVries proposed that mutations, which are large differences arising suddenly in a population, drive evolution. He based this on his work on evening primrose. Garden pea is the trap because it is associated with Mendel's work on inheritable factors.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, 16% of individuals show the recessive phenotype (aa). What is the frequency of heterozygous (Aa) individuals?
questions.explanation: Here $q^2 = 0.16$, so $q = 0.4$ and $p = 0.6$. The heterozygote frequency is $2pq = 2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.48$. The value 0.24 comes from forgetting the factor 2, and 0.36 is $p^2$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the early earth are correct?
(i) The earth had a well-formed atmosphere right from the time of its formation.
(ii) UV radiation from the sun split water into hydrogen and oxygen.
(iii) The ozone layer was formed after oxygen became available on the early earth.
(iv) Oxygen combined with methane and ammonia to form water and CO$_2$.
(v) Life appeared about 500 million years before the formation of the earth.
questions.explanation: Statements (ii), (iii) and (iv) are correct. The early earth had no atmosphere at first, so (i) is wrong. Life appeared 500 million years after the earth formed, not before, so (v) is wrong.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider two comparisons:
(1) The beaks of a seed-eating and an insectivorous Darwin's finch, both modified from the beak of a common ancestral finch.
(2) The overall body form of the Tasmanian wolf and the placental wolf, which belong to two separate radiations.
Which evolutionary patterns do comparisons (1) and (2) illustrate, respectively?
options: Convergent evolution; divergent evolution
Divergent evolution; convergent evolution
Divergent evolution in both
Convergent evolution in both
questions.explanation: Within one radiation, a shared ancestral structure is modified in different directions, which is divergent evolution (homology). Members of two different radiations becoming alike in similar habitats is convergent evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the early earth, as described in NCERT, is INCORRECT?
options: Initially there was no atmosphere, and water vapour, $CH_4$, $CO_2$ and $NH_3$ released from the molten mass covered the surface.
UV rays from the sun split water into hydrogen and oxygen, and the lighter $H_2$ escaped.
Free oxygen released by the splitting of water built up as the main gas, so the atmosphere became oxidising before life appeared.
As the earth cooled, water vapour fell as rain and filled the depressions to form oceans.
questions.explanation: The oxygen released did not accumulate as a free gas. It combined with ammonia and methane to form water, $CO_2$ and other compounds, so the early atmosphere remained reducing ($CH_4$, $NH_3$). The other three statements match the NCERT account.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 belonged to a hominid that lived about 1.5 million years ago, had a brain capacity of about 900 cc and probably ate meat. Which hominid was this?
options: Homo habilis
Australopithecus
Homo erectus
Neanderthal man
questions.explanation: NCERT describes the Java fossils of 1891 as Homo erectus, which lived about 1.5 mya, had a brain of about 900 cc and probably ate meat. Homo habilis had a smaller brain of 650–800 cc and probably did not eat meat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the idea of 'panspermia', which some astronomers still favour, how did life arise on earth?
options: Living organisms arose from decaying straw and mud
Units of life called spores were transferred to earth from elsewhere in space
Organic molecules formed from inorganic constituents in the primitive oceans
All species were created in their present form about 4000 years ago
questions.explanation: Panspermia holds that spores, the units of life, travelled to different planets, including earth, from outer space. The other options describe spontaneous generation, chemical evolution and special creation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Darwin observed many varieties of small black birds, later called Darwin's finches, during his voyage. Where did he observe them?
options: Malay Archipelago
Galapagos Islands
Australian mainland
Madagascar
questions.explanation: Darwin saw the finches on the Galapagos Islands and proposed that all the varieties evolved on the island itself. The Malay Archipelago is linked with Alfred Wallace, not with the finches.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
B. Sweet potato and potato
C. Different breeds of dogs
D. Similar proteins and genes performing a given function in diverse organisms
List-II
I. Biochemical evidence of shared ancestry
II. Analogy in plants
III. Homology in plants
IV. Artificial selection by man
Choose the correct answer.
options: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
questions.explanation:
The pairings are as follows:
- Thorn and tendril share an origin, so they are homologous (A-III).
- Sweet potato and potato differ in origin but share a function, so they are analogous (B-II).
- Dog breeds were produced by human breeding (C-IV).
- Similar proteins and genes give biochemical clues to common ancestry (D-I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about dinosaurs and early mammals is INCORRECT according to NCERT?
options: Tyrannosaurus rex, the biggest dinosaur, was about 20 feet tall and had huge dagger-like teeth
NCERT concludes that dinosaurs were wiped out about 65 mya solely because of climatic changes
The first mammals were shrew-like, and their fossils are small in size
Early mammals were viviparous and better at sensing and avoiding danger than reptiles
questions.explanation: NCERT says the true reason for dinosaur extinction is unknown. Some suggest climatic change, others suggest most dinosaurs evolved into birds, and the truth may lie in between, so 'solely climatic change' is wrong.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the Hardy–Weinberg principle, what is the term for the total genes and their alleles in a population remaining constant from generation to generation?
options: Gene flow
Genetic drift
Genetic equilibrium
Founder effect
questions.explanation: When allele frequencies stay stable across generations and the gene pool remains constant, the population is said to be in genetic equilibrium. Gene flow, genetic drift and the founder effect are all processes that disturb this equilibrium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Embryos of all vertebrates develop a row of vestigial gill slits just behind the head. In which group of adult vertebrates are these gill slits functional organs?
options: Amphibians
Reptiles
Mammals
Fishes
questions.explanation: Gill slits work as functional organs only in adult fish. They are not found in any other adult vertebrate, including amphibians.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The idea of 'Panspermia', still favoured by some astronomers, proposes that:
options: units of life called spores were transferred to different planets, including earth
life arose spontaneously from rotting and decaying matter
all living species were created as such and have remained unchanged
life arose on earth through chemical evolution in a reducing atmosphere
questions.explanation: Panspermia, traced to early Greek thinkers, holds that life came from outer space as spores. Option 2 describes spontaneous generation and option 3 describes special creation. Option 4 is the Oparin–Haldane view.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about industrial melanism in moths in England is correct?
options: In rural areas without industrialisation, melanic moths outnumbered white-winged moths
Lichens grew abundantly on tree trunks in polluted areas
After industrialisation, white-winged moths were completely wiped out
Predators readily spot a moth that contrasts with its background
questions.explanation: The proposed explanation was that predators pick out moths that contrast with the bark, so camouflaged moths survive. Melanic moths stayed rare in rural areas, and lichens do not grow in polluted areas. No variant is ever completely wiped out.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Analogous organs arise due to:
options: divergent evolution
artificial selection
genetic drift
convergent evolution
questions.explanation: Analogous organs, such as the wings of birds and butterflies, perform similar functions but have different structures and origins. They develop when unrelated groups adapt to similar needs, which is convergent evolution.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q6)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fossils are generally found in:
options: Sedimentary rocks
Igneous rocks
Metamorphic rocks
Any type of rock
questions.explanation: Fossils form when remains of organisms are buried in layers of sediment that harden into rock. The intense heat involved in forming igneous and metamorphic rocks destroys such remains.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q11)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Australopithecines
(B) Homo habilis
(C) Homo erectus
(D) Neanderthal man
List-II
(I) Brain capacity 650–800 cc; probably did not eat meat
(II) Brain capacity about 1400 cc; lived in near east and central Asia
(III) Hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruit
(IV) Brain capacity about 900 cc; probably ate meat
Choose the correct answer:
options: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II
questions.explanation: Australopithecines in East African grasslands hunted with stone weapons but mainly ate fruit. Homo habilis had 650–800 cc and probably did not eat meat, Homo erectus had about 900 cc and probably ate meat, and Neanderthals had 1400 cc. The common trap is swapping the diets of H. habilis and H. erectus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following were reported to form in Miller's experiment or in similar later experiments simulating early-earth conditions?
Amino acids, sugars, nitrogen bases, pigments, fats, membrane-bound cells, self-replicating bacteria
questions.explanation: Miller obtained amino acids, and others obtained sugars, nitrogen bases, pigments and fats, making five. No cells or living organisms were formed; these experiments supported only chemical evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Appearance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is an example of:
options: adaptive radiation
transduction
pre-existing variation in the population
divergent evolution
questions.explanation: A few bacteria already carry resistance before the antibiotic is used. The antibiotic kills the susceptible ones, so the resistant variants survive and multiply.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q8)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Homo habilis
B. Homo erectus
C. Neanderthal man
D. Dryopithecus
List-II
I. Fossils found in Java in 1891; brain about 900 cc
II. Brain capacity 650-800 cc; probably did not eat meat
III. More ape-like primate existing about 15 mya
IV. Brain about 1400 cc; buried their dead
options: A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation: Homo habilis had a brain of 650-800 cc and was probably not a meat-eater. Homo erectus, known from the 1891 Java fossils, had a brain of about 900 cc. Neanderthals had a brain of about 1400 cc and buried their dead, while Dryopithecus was the more ape-like primate of about 15 mya.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hugo deVries proposed the idea of mutation as the cause of evolution. On which organism was his work based?
options: Garden pea
Evening primrose
Snapdragon
Fruit fly
questions.explanation: deVries put forward the mutation idea from his studies on evening primrose in the first decade of the twentieth century. Garden pea was Mendel's plant, not deVries'.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following pairs are homologous?
1. Forelimbs of whale and bat
2. Heart of a frog and heart of a human
3. Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
4. Wings of butterfly and bird
5. Flippers of penguin and dolphin
6. Sweet potato and potato
7. Brain of a fish and brain of a human
options: Three
Four
Five
Two
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2, 3 and 7 are homologous: mammalian forelimbs, vertebrate hearts, Bougainvillea thorn with Cucurbita tendril, and vertebrate brains. Pairs 4, 5 and 6 are NCERT's examples of analogy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three connotations of the theory of special creation?
options: All living organisms seen today were created as such
The diversity was always the same since creation and will remain the same in future
The earth is about 4000 years old
The earth is billions of years old and life forms have changed gradually
questions.explanation: Special creation holds that species were created as such, that diversity is unchanging, and that the earth is about 4000 years old. A billions-of-years-old earth with gradually changing life forms is the conclusion that challenged special creation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A graph shows the number of individuals plotted against the value of a heritable trait. Before selection, the curve is bell-shaped with a single peak at the mean. After many generations, the number of individuals near the mean has fallen, and two peaks have appeared at both ends of the distribution. Which type of natural selection does this represent?
options: Stabilising selection
Directional selection
Disruptive selection
Genetic drift
questions.explanation: Disruptive selection favours peripheral trait values at both ends of the curve, which produces two peaks. Stabilising selection increases individuals at the mean, and directional selection shifts the single peak to one side.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sweet potato and potato are cited as an example of analogy because
options: both are modified roots that store food
both are modified stems that store food
sweet potato is a modified root and potato is a modified stem, yet both store food
sweet potato is a modified stem and potato is a modified root, and they perform different functions
questions.explanation: The two storage organs come from different structures (a root in sweet potato, a stem in potato) but serve the same function. This makes them analogous. The trap is reversing which organ is the root and which is the stem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The placental wolf and the Tasmanian wolf look similar even though one is a placental mammal and the other a marsupial.
Reason (R): Their similarity is due to divergent evolution of the same structure from a recent common ancestor.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The two wolves do resemble each other, so A is true. However, the resemblance arose through convergent evolution, as placental and marsupial lineages each radiated in Australia and produced similar forms. R wrongly attributes this to divergent evolution from a common ancestor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: According to deVries, mutation caused speciation in a single large step, which he called saltation.
Statement II: For Darwin, evolution was a gradual process based on small heritable variations.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: deVries held that a single-step large mutation (saltation) causes speciation. Darwin viewed evolution as gradual and driven by small, directional heritable variations. Both statements are therefore correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bacteria resistant to antibiotics and pests resistant to pesticides now appear within months or years rather than centuries. NCERT describes this kind of evolution as
options: Evolution by anthropogenic action
Saltation caused by a single large mutation
Adaptive radiation from an ancestral stock
Evolution by use and disuse of organs
questions.explanation: Human actions such as heavy use of antibiotics, herbicides and pesticides select resistant varieties on a short time scale. NCERT calls this evolution by anthropogenic action. Saltation, adaptive radiation and use and disuse are unrelated ideas.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Homo habilis
(B) Homo erectus
(C) Neanderthal man
(D) Ramapithecus
List-II:
(i) Brain about 1400 cc; buried their dead
(ii) Brain 650-800 cc; probably did not eat meat
(iii) Brain about 900 cc; probably ate meat
(iv) Man-like primate existing about 15 mya
Choose the correct option.
options: A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(iii), B-(ii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(ii), B-(i), C-(iii), D-(iv)
A-(iv), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(ii)
questions.explanation: Homo habilis had 650-800 cc and was probably not a meat-eater. Homo erectus had about 900 cc and ate meat. Neanderthals had 1400 cc and buried their dead. Ramapithecus was the more man-like primate of about 15 mya.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are mammals that live wholly in water, as mentioned in NCERT?
Whales, Ichthyosaurs, Dolphins, Coelacanth, Seals, Sea cows
questions.explanation: Whales, dolphins, seals and sea cows are the aquatic mammals NCERT names, which makes four. Ichthyosaurs were fish-like reptiles and the Coelacanth is a lobefin fish.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following can disturb Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium in a population?
Gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination, natural selection, random mating, large population size
options: Three
Four
Five
Six
questions.explanation: NCERT lists five factors that alter allele frequencies: gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination and natural selection. Random mating and a large population size are conditions that help maintain the equilibrium rather than disturb it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The earth, a member of the solar system of the Milky Way galaxy, is believed to have been formed about:
options: 13.8 billion years ago
2000 million years ago
4.5 billion years ago
3 billion years ago
questions.explanation: The earth formed about 4.5 billion years ago. 13.8 billion years is the age of the universe, and 2000 mya is roughly when the first cellular life appeared.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological order, from oldest to most recent:
(A) Fish-like reptiles such as Ichthyosaurs evolved
(B) Invertebrates were formed and active
(C) First cellular forms of life appeared
(D) Dinosaurs suddenly disappeared
(E) Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus existed
options: C, B, A, D, E
C, A, B, D, E
B, C, A, E, D
C, B, D, A, E
questions.explanation: The order is: first cells (about 2000 mya), invertebrates (by 500 mya), Ichthyosaurs (about 200 mya), disappearance of dinosaurs (about 65 mya), and Dryopithecus/Ramapithecus (about 15 mya). The key trap is placing the dinosaur extinction before the fish-like reptiles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Ichthyosaurs were fish-like reptiles that evolved, probably around 200 mya, from land reptiles that went back into water.
Statement II: Specimens of the first amphibians that evolved from lobefins are still alive today in the form of frogs and salamanders.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Statement I matches NCERT. Statement II is wrong because no specimens of the first amphibians are left; frogs and salamanders are only their modern descendants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the age of reptiles, which plants slowly fell and formed coal deposits?
options: Giant ferns (pteridophytes)
Seaweeds
Flowering plants (angiosperms)
Mosses (bryophytes)
questions.explanation: Giant ferns, which are pteridophytes, existed during the period of reptile dominance and slowly fell to form coal deposits. Seaweeds were early aquatic forms, not coal-forming land plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In England, collections made in 1920 showed more dark-winged (melanised) moths than white-winged moths, reversing the proportion seen in the 1850s.
Reason (R): Industrial soot darkened tree trunks and the whitish lichens disappeared, so dark moths were camouflaged from predators while white moths were easily spotted.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: After industrialisation, the darkened bark gave melanised moths better camouflage, so predators selectively removed white moths. This is exactly why the proportion of dark moths rose. Note that neither variant was completely wiped out.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Alfred Wallace reached conclusions similar to Darwin's on natural selection at around the same time. Where did Wallace carry out his work as a naturalist?
options: Galapagos Islands
Malay Archipelago
Australian island continent
East African grasslands
questions.explanation: Wallace worked in the Malay Archipelago. The Galapagos Islands are linked with Darwin's finches, which is the common trap.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is used as an atmospheric pollution indicator?
options: Lepidoptera
Lichens
Lycopersicon
Lycopodium
questions.explanation: Lichens are very sensitive to air pollutants, especially SO$_2$, and do not grow in polluted areas. Their presence or absence therefore indicates air quality.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sweet potato and potato are both food-storing organs, but they are cited as an example of analogy. The reason is that:
options: Sweet potato is a modified root, whereas potato is a modified stem
Both are modified stems that share a common origin
Both are modified roots that perform the same function
Sweet potato is a modified stem, whereas potato is a modified root
questions.explanation: Sweet potato is a root modification and potato is a stem modification. They have different origins but serve the same storage function, which makes them analogous. Option 4 swaps the origins and is a common slip.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: According to Oparin and Haldane, the first form of life could have come from pre-existing non-living organic molecules such as RNA and proteins, preceded by chemical evolution.
Statement II: The first cellular forms of life, which arose about 2000 million years ago, were probably multicellular and lived both on land and in water.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.explanation: Statement I correctly summarises the Oparin–Haldane view of abiogenesis through chemical evolution. Statement II is wrong because the first cells were probably single-celled and all life forms were then confined to water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the moth collections made in the same area of England, which type of moth was more common in the collection made in 1920, after industrialisation?
options: White-winged moths
Dark-winged (melanised) moths
White-winged and dark-winged moths in equal numbers
Only white-winged moths, because dark moths had been wiped out
questions.explanation: The 1850s collection had more white-winged moths, and by 1920 this proportion had reversed in favour of melanised moths. Neither variant was completely wiped out.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): According to Darwin, individuals better fit in an environment are selected by nature.
Reason (R): Darwinian fitness refers ultimately to reproductive fitness, so better-fit individuals leave more progeny than others.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Better-fit individuals leave more progeny, so their characters increase in later generations. This greater reproductive output is exactly what Darwin meant by being selected by nature.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are listed as factors that affect Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium?
Gene migration, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination, natural selection, constancy of allele frequencies, binomial expansion $(p+q)^2$
questions.explanation: The five factors that affect Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium are gene migration (gene flow), genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination and natural selection. Constancy of allele frequencies is the equilibrium state itself, not a disturbing factor. The binomial expansion is simply the mathematical form of the principle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In England, the proportion of dark-winged (melanised) moths rose after industrialisation. Which observation best supports the explanation that this happened because of predation against a contrasting background?
options: In rural areas where industrialisation did not occur, the count of melanic moths remained low
White-winged moths were completely wiped out from industrial areas
Lichens grew more thickly on tree trunks in industrial areas
Dark-winged moths appeared only after 1920 as fresh mutations
questions.explanation: Melanic moths stayed rare where trunks were not darkened by soot, which links their success to camouflage on dark trunks. No variant was completely wiped out, and lichens do not grow in polluted areas.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to Darwin, the 'fitness' of an individual or population refers ultimately and only to its
options: physical strength
length of life span
reproductive fitness
ability to escape predators
questions.explanation: Darwinian fitness means reproductive fitness, that is, leaving more progeny than others. Strength, longevity or escaping predators count only if they lead to more offspring.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs represents analogous organs?
options: Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
Heart of a fish and heart of a human
Eye of an octopus and eye of a mammal
Forelimb of a bat and forelimb of a whale
questions.explanation: The octopus eye and the mammalian eye do the same job but are not anatomically similar in origin, so they are analogous. The other three pairs are homologous. The trap is the Bougainvillea–Cucurbita pair, which NCERT gives as a plant example of homology.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Charles Darwin
(B) Alfred Wallace
(C) Lamarck
(D) Thomas Malthus
List-II:
(I) Work on populations
(II) Voyage on H.M.S. Beagle
(III) Use and disuse of organs
(IV) Malay Archipelago
Choose the correct answer.
options: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
questions.explanation: Darwin made his observations during the H.M.S. Beagle voyage, and Wallace worked in the Malay Archipelago. Lamarck proposed use and disuse of organs, and Malthus's work on populations probably influenced Darwin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, what was the original feeding type from which the other forms of Darwin's finches with altered beaks arose?
options: Insectivorous
Vegetarian
Seed-eating
Nectar-feeding
questions.explanation: The ancestral finches had seed-eating features. Altered beaks then arose that allowed some forms to become insectivorous and others vegetarian, so these are derived forms, not the starting point.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs represents homologous organs in plants?
options: Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
Tuber of sweet potato and tuber of potato
Wings of butterfly and wings of birds
Flippers of penguins and flippers of dolphins
questions.explanation: The thorn of Bougainvillea and the tendril of Cucurbita have the same basic origin but perform different functions, so they are homologous. Sweet potato and potato are an analogous plant example, and the other two pairs are animal examples of analogy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Homology
(b) Analogy
(c) Biochemical evidence
(d) Artificial selection
List-II
(i) Similar proteins and genes performing a given function in diverse organisms
(ii) Breeds of dogs
(iii) Brains of different vertebrates
(iv) Eye of octopus and eye of mammal
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Vertebrate brains are homologous and the octopus and mammal eyes are analogous. Shared proteins and genes are biochemical evidence of common ancestry, and dog breeds come from artificial selection. Option 1 reverses the homology and analogy examples.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Stabilising selection
(B) Directional selection
(C) Disruptive selection
(D) Founder effect
List-II
(I) More individuals acquire a character value other than the mean
(II) A drifted population becomes so different that it forms a new species
(III) More individuals acquire the mean character value
(IV) More individuals acquire peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve
Choose the correct answer:
options: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II
questions.explanation: Stabilising selection favours the mean, and directional selection shifts the population towards a value other than the mean. Disruptive selection favours both extremes, and in the founder effect a drifted population becomes the founders of a new species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Flippers of penguins and dolphins resemble each other because both groups inherited flippers from a common aquatic ancestor that possessed them.
Statement II: A similar habitat can lead to selection of similar adaptive features in different groups of organisms, directed towards the same function.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Penguin and dolphin flippers are analogous. They are a product of convergent evolution in a similar aquatic habitat, not inheritance from a flippered common ancestor. So Statement I is wrong and Statement II correctly states the cause of analogy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with alleles A and a, and 16% of its individuals are homozygous recessive (aa).
Statement I: The frequency of the dominant allele A in this population is 0.6.
Statement II: The expected frequency of heterozygous (Aa) individuals in this population is 0.24.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Since $q^2 = 0.16$, $q = 0.4$ and $p = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$, so Statement I is correct. The heterozygote frequency is $2pq = 2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.48$, not 0.24. The value 0.24 comes from forgetting the factor of 2 in $2pq$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Analysis of meteorite content is considered supporting evidence for chemical evolution.
Reason (R): Meteorites have been found to contain compounds similar to those formed in Miller-type experiments, suggesting that similar processes occur elsewhere in space.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation: Meteorites contain organic compounds like those produced in laboratory simulations. This indicates that the abiotic synthesis of biomolecules is not unique to the lab, which is why the evidence supports chemical evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following pairs represent analogous structures?
(i) Wings of butterfly and wings of bird
(ii) Eye of octopus and eye of mammal
(iii) Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
(iv) Flippers of penguin and flippers of dolphin
(v) Forelimbs of whale and forelimbs of bat
(vi) Sweet potato and potato
(vii) Hearts of different vertebrates
questions.explanation: Pairs (i), (ii), (iv) and (vi) are analogous: they are anatomically different but perform similar functions, which is convergent evolution. The Bougainvillea thorn and Cucurbita tendril, mammalian forelimbs and vertebrate hearts are homologous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The thorn of Bougainvillea and the tendril of Cucurbita are homologous structures and point to common ancestry.
Statement II: The wings of a butterfly and those of a bird are homologous because they perform the same function.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Thorn and tendril share a common origin but serve different functions, so they are homologous structures produced by divergent evolution. Butterfly and bird wings perform the same function but differ in anatomy, so they are analogous structures produced by convergent evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: $(p+q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$ represents an equation used in:
options: population genetics
mendelian genetics
biometrics
molecular genetics
questions.explanation: This is the Hardy-Weinberg equation. It relates allele frequencies to genotype frequencies in a population and is fundamental to population genetics.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q7)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct according to the NCERT account of evolution?
(a) The first organisms to invade land were animals, and plants followed them later.
(b) Giant ferns (pteridophytes) fell and slowly formed coal deposits.
(c) The first mammals were shrew-like and protected their unborn young inside the mother's body.
(d) When South America joined North America, South American mammals resembling horse and hippopotamus overrode the North American fauna.
(e) Lobefins evolved directly into the first reptiles.
(f) Continental drift allowed the pouched mammals of Australia to survive due to lack of competition from other mammals.
questions.explanation:
Statements (b), (c) and (f) are correct, so the answer is 3. The other three are wrong for these reasons:
- (a): plants invaded land first.
- (d): the North American fauna overrode the South American mammals, not the reverse.
- (e): lobefins gave rise to the first amphibians, not the first reptiles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus were hairy and walked like gorillas and chimpanzees.
(ii) Man-like primates that walked in eastern Africa about 3–4 mya were taller than 6 feet.
(iii) Homo erectus fossils were discovered in Java in 1891.
(iv) Homo sapiens arose in Africa and moved across continents to develop into distinct races.
(v) Agriculture began about 18,000 years ago.
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct. The primates of 3–4 mya were probably not taller than 4 feet, though they walked upright. About 18,000 years ago is the age of prehistoric cave art, while agriculture came about 10,000 years ago.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The prehistoric cave paintings that can be seen at the Bhimbetka rock shelter are located in which district of India?
options: Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh
Aurangabad district, Maharashtra
Bellary district, Karnataka
Sagar district, Madhya Pradesh
questions.explanation: NCERT cites the Bhimbetka rock shelter in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh as a site of cave paintings by prehistoric humans. Prehistoric cave art developed about 18,000 years ago.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Louis Pasteur's experiment with 'killed yeast' in pre-sterilised flasks and in flasks open to air led to which conclusion?
options: Life arises from decaying matter such as straw and mud.
Life on earth arrived as spores from other planets.
Organic molecules form from inorganic constituents under reducing conditions.
Life comes only from pre-existing life.
questions.explanation: No life appeared in the sterilised flask, while organisms arose in the flask open to air. This showed that living things come only from pre-existing life and dismissed spontaneous generation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: For a gene with two alleles A (frequency $p$) and a (frequency $q$) in a population at Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, what is the maximum possible frequency of heterozygotes (Aa)?
questions.explanation: Since $p + q = 1$, the heterozygote frequency $2pq$ is greatest when $p = q = 0.5$, giving $2 \times 0.5 \times 0.5 = 0.5$. The value 0.25 is $pq$ without the factor 2. A frequency of 1.00 is impossible because $p^2$ and $q^2$ cannot both be zero when $p = q$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological order, from earliest to latest:
(i) Appearance of cells able to release $O_2$ by splitting water using solar energy
(ii) Invertebrates formed and active
(iii) Land reptiles returned to water and gave rise to Ichthyosaurs
(iv) Sudden disappearance of dinosaurs
(v) Fish with stout, strong fins moving onto land, leading to the first amphibians
questions.explanation: $O_2$-releasing cells were among the early cellular forms (about 2000 mya), and invertebrates were active by about 500 mya. Lobefins moved onto land about 350 mya, Ichthyosaurs arose about 200 mya, and dinosaurs vanished about 65 mya.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The embryological evidence for evolution proposed by Ernst Haeckel was disapproved.
Reason (R): Karl Ernst von Baer observed that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Haeckel argued that vertebrate embryos show features, such as gill slits, of other adult forms. Von Baer's careful study showed that embryos never pass through adult stages of other animals, and this is exactly why Haeckel's proposal was rejected.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct option.
List-I:
A. Homo habilis
B. Homo erectus
C. Neanderthal man
D. Ramapithecus
List-II:
I. Brain about 1400 cc; buried their dead
II. Primate of about 15 mya, more man-like than Dryopithecus
III. Brain 650–800 cc; probably did not eat meat
IV. Brain about 900 cc; fossils found in Java (1891)
options: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
questions.explanation: Homo habilis had a brain of 650–800 cc and probably did not eat meat. Homo erectus (about 900 cc) is known from the Java fossils, and Neanderthals (1400 cc) buried their dead. Ramapithecus was the more man-like primate of about 15 mya, whereas Dryopithecus was more ape-like.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Palaeontological evidences for evolution refer to the:
options: development of embryo
homologous organs
fossils
analogous organs.
questions.explanation: Palaeontology is the study of fossils. Fossils preserved in rock layers of different ages show how life forms changed over time.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q4)

questions.subject: Biology
